clue.text: Told to waive part of the fibre diet

definitions.meaning: said out loud, 'waive' is 'wave', and to wave a weapon or flag about is the sense wanted
a bowl of bran, the roughage people eat for fibre, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone is being instructed to give up a portion of their high-fibre eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told' makes 'waive' heard as 'wave', so the first definition is 'to wave'; the second splits the word as BRAN DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword is to wave it about; a dish of bran is the classic fibre-rich breakfast.

clue.text: Women who should be sent packing?

definitions.text: Women who should be sent packing?

parts.words: Women who should be sent packing?
parts.note: an old derogatory word for disreputable women is also the plural of luggage, which is what gets packed

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for cheeky or worthless women matches the word for luggage, which is naturally packed.

clue.text: Warn the head to have vigilance

parts.note: to alert someone is to warn them
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Tell the boss to keep watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' reads as the boss; it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and wary is the state of being on guard.

clue.text: American lawyer has middle-age spread? It's a fact

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
a tum is a belly, the paunch of middle age

explanation.surface: A US attorney's paunch is noted as undeniable.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of information or given item of evidence is a known truth.

clue.text: Disconcert the Society party man

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Upset the man throwing the society party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party man' suggests a socialite; the party is the Mad Hatter's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset badly is to break someone's composure into pieces.

clue.text: Signal to assume the role of a swindler

parts.note: to be someone, as in 'you be the doctor', is to play that part
a con is a confidence trickster, a swindler

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a sign that you will pose as a fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire lit on a hill to warn of danger was a signal light.

clue.text: Urges to install machines — they bear fruit

indicators.note: to install something is to set it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: to egg on is to urge, so eggs means urges
plant is industrial machinery

explanation.surface: Someone presses for machinery to be fitted, which will be productive.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine plants are fruit-bearers: the purple vegetable is botanically a berry.

clue.text: Punished many a man

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: Lots of people punished a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten with a stick was a traditional school punishment.

clue.text: Made a home for a good man who's impoverished

indicators.note: the good man is held within the poor state, as 'who is' places him inside it

parts.note: to be in need is to be poor
ST, for saint, is crosswordese for a good man

explanation.surface: Someone gave a house to a worthy but penniless man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a home for' reads as charity; the definition is just 'Made a home', as birds do.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle in by building nests, so to have done so is to have settled.

clue.text: Dull dog roughed up in a filthy place

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the filthy place

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a byword for a filthy place

indicators.note: a dog that is roughed up is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boring dog is mistreated in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'filthy place' is the usual crossword pigsty; 'roughed up' scrambles the dog, and 'in' tucks the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy food is stolid, and so a heavy, uninspired thing is tedious.

clue.text: Of remarkable ability, like Peter, say

definitions.meaning: Peter I of Russia carried that epithet, as did Alfred and Alexander

explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding talent is a grand one, and Tsar Peter I is known by that royal epithet.

clue.text: Sadly no guts in a general under Alexander

indicators.note: the sorry state of the words 'no guts in a' signals they are to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A lament that one of Alexander's commanders lacked courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like comment on the cowardly general, but it is the anagram signal for NO GUTS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigonus One-Eye was a Macedonian commander who served Alexander the Great and later became a king.

clue.text: Chap with car rug is equipped to go on own

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a mat is a small rug
Ed is a common short man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man with a travelling blanket for his vehicle is ready to set off alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-operating machine is one that runs by itself without human control.

clue.text: Physicist's dwelling

definitions.meaning: Sir Oliver ..., British physicist and radio pioneer
a small house, such as a gatekeeper's cottage

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Oliver Lodge was a physicist noted for radio work; a gatekeeper's cottage is a small house of that name.

clue.text: German prince who has the franchise

definitions.meaning: a prince of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to choose the emperor
one with the right to vote

explanation.definitionFit: Princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor held that title; anyone with the vote is likewise a chooser.

clue.text: Keen ditch worker

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant, especially a worker ant, is crosswordese for worker

explanation.surface: An eager labourer digging ditches.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen in the sense of sharp or incisive, as in cutting criticism.

clue.text: One drawn into being an American?

definitions.text: One drawn into being an American?

parts.words: One drawn into being an American?
parts.note: read as one who has been yanked, by the -ee ending as in employee, the word is also slang for a US citizen

explanation.definitionFit: Yank is slang for a person from the USA, and the longer form, read as 'one yanked', fits 'one drawn'.

clue.text: Count transposes a mere tune

indicators.note: a transposed tune is shifted, and here the letters of 'a mere tune' are shifted around

explanation.surface: A nobleman arranges a simple melody in a new key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman doing the transposing; it is the verb, to list.
explanation.definitionFit: To list one by one or tally is to count.

clue.text: Enid's vexed with Les doing nothing

indicators.note: vexed means troubled or stirred up, so the names are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the name and its S are fodder

explanation.surface: Enid is annoyed with Les for lazing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness or inactivity is the state of being unoccupied.

clue.text: Oral agreement to a rise

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word for agreement is heard rather than seen

parts.note: assent is agreement or consent

explanation.surface: Spoken consent is given to a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rise' sounds like a pay rise, but it is a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb up a slope is an upward movement or rise.

clue.text: The church captured the north for that reason

indicators.note: captured means the north is held between the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: The Church took over the north of the country for a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning 'from that' or 'therefore', an old word for drawing a conclusion.

clue.text: Ring for report by engineers

indicators.note: by means next to, so the noise sits beside the engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a report is a loud noise, a sound

explanation.surface: Telephone the military engineers to make a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call; it means to echo loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo or reverberate loudly is to ring out.

clue.text: Arrange rise, owing the rest

indicators.note: arrange tells you to put the letters of 'rise' in a new order

parts.note: due means owed or owing

explanation.surface: Organise a pay increase, with the remainder still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the remainder.

clue.text: Superior sailor and his girl

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Bess is a girl's name, the sailor's girlfriend

explanation.surface: A higher-ranking seaman and his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like an adjective; it is a Mother Superior, head of a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a nunnery is called its Mother Superior.

clue.text: Kind of English degree — so simple

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic is Latin for 'thus' or 'so', used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A plain English qualification described as easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of English' is a second hint: Basic English is a simplified 850-word form of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary or plain things are fundamental and uncomplicated.

clue.text: I may be in the lead as a music maker

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for lead

parts.note: the star is the lead performer

explanation.surface: A performer hopes to land the starring role as a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian stringed instrument with a long neck makes music.

clue.text: Get away from here before wheels get broken first

indicators.note: first says the shuffled wheels come at the front, ahead of the other piece
wheels that get broken are smashed out of shape, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Escape from this place before the cart's wheels give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away' tempts as the definition, but 'get' belongs with 'broken' as the anagram signal; 'first' says the scrambled wheels lead and 'before' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere other than this place is in another location.

clue.text: Bird notes on an English river

annotationWithheld.why: Bird notes on an English river (5) as printed for WADER: no reading found builds W from the clue, and no English river WAR or WR fits; the wordplay is unclear
annotationWithheld.clue: Bird notes on an English river

clue.text: Delighted to find the fourth turnstile

parts.note: a turnstile is a gated way in, an entrance
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to discover the fourth gate at a ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being charmed or enchanted means being filled with delight.

clue.text: Sea farer gets the bird

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan navigator; the same word names a male duck.

clue.text: Small dainty person runs into animosity

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the word for animosity

parts.note: spite is malice or animosity
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tiny, delicate person stumbles into some hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf or fairy is a tiny dainty being.

clue.text: Matchless as the common folk are

definitions.meaning: commoners have no titled nobles among them, read as 'without lords'

explanation.definitionFit: Something unequalled has no rivals; commoners are literally without lords, the British peerage.
